Chapter 7: The Art of Collaboration and Building Creative Teams
You know, nobody really makes it on their own. Behind every sketch, every show-stopping moment, there’s always a team—writers, performers, producers, crew—each person bringing their own kind of magic and, let’s be honest, their quirks too.
Now, stepping into a leadership role, she discovers something important: collaboration isn’t just about getting along. It’s a real blend of art and science.
Of course, the process is rarely smooth. Creative folks are passionate, opinionated, and sometimes, well... a little stubborn. Egos can clash, ideas compete, and every now and then, tempers flare. Some days, it honestly feels like herding cats. The room gets thick with frustration, and doubt creeps in.
But then there are those other days—the days when everything just clicks. Maybe it’s a brainstorm that turns into laughter, a rehearsal so good it feels like magic, or a late-night rewrite that takes an okay sketch and turns it into something unforgettable.
Over time, she learns that the best teams aren’t built on who’s the smartest or who gets the biggest laugh. It all comes down to trust and respect. It’s about building a space where everyone feels safe to take risks, to fail, and to try again. She never forgets her early days in improv—the importance of really listening, of saying “yes, and,” of always having each other’s backs. Those lessons? They become the heart of how she leads.
There’s this moment, late in the season, when a new writer pitches an idea that sounds risky—maybe even a little foolish. The room gets quiet, waiting for her response. She catches the uncertainty in the writer’s eyes, that hope that maybe, just maybe, this idea will land. She takes a deep breath, remembers her own first pitches, and she says, “Let’s try it.”
The sketch doesn’t really work out. But something more important happens—the writer grows bolder, more confident. The team learns something huge: failure isn’t the end. In fact, creativity thrives when people feel encouraged to take those leaps.
As time goes on, she makes a name for herself—not just for her own talent, but for bringing out the best in everyone around her. She mentors new performers, lifts up all kinds of voices, and insists on kindness as a rule, not an exception.
The work is tough, but the rewards are real. The team feels like a family. The show becomes a reflection of their shared experience—richer and more vibrant because of everyone’s contribution. And her legacy? It goes way beyond her own achievements; it’s about the creative community she’s helped to build.
